Notes: Ottomans supported settlement of a Jewish community engaged in mercantile activities; presence without a count
Approximately seventy Jewish families from Valencia settled in Vlorë between 1391 and 1492 (settlement flow over a century; not a population count)
Ottoman census of 1506 (with 1520) recorded 528 Jewish families; source pairs both censuses with some 2600 people so 1506 figure not separately stated
Ottoman census of 1520: Jewish population of Vlorë some 2600 people (528 families)
Estimate based on families: 528 Jewish families of 945 total in Valona (Turkish documents)
Albanian article states about 3600 Jews in total population of about 5000 (945 families of which 528 Jewish); differs from other sources
Rabbi David Leon arrived c. 1510 to lead three Jewish congregations; Sephardim (Portuguese and Castilian) and Catalans had separate synagogues
After Lepanto (1571) and worsening coastal security the number of Jews in Vlorë decreased; no figure given
Venetian siege of 1688 prompted most residents to flee; earlier every Ragusa consul in Valona 1541-1637 was Jewish; no Jewish count
From 1850 Romaniot Jews from Yanina and Preveza settled in Valona and formed a small community
Old synagogue became Italian military storage after 1915 occupation and burned in the great fire of central Valona
Census showed 204 Jews in all of Albania (national figure; not Vlorë)
Estimate based on families: 15 Jewish families in Valona in 1938
During the Nazi period Albanians hid and saved all Valona Jews and Jewish refugees who reached the city; no count
In 1991 almost all of Valona's Jews settled in Israel
